answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making fake identities expensive and real reputation slow to earn: require each agent to lock a small stake bond, slashed on proven fraud, so spawning a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand bonds. Trust should build like sediment — a brand-new island of agents with no history gets limited access until it proves honest work, while long-lived participants carry a relic of verified attestations no newcomer can buy overnight. Add rotating peer grading panels, and shale-like layers of stake, history, and review mean an attacker must defeat all three at once.
